Subject: Clarion demo: performance eligibility criteria & mutual action plan

Hi Ayesha / Clarion team —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side with the performance items we agreed to validate and the proposed next steps (MAP):

1) Latency targets
   - 95th pct target for single-turn API (tokenized transcript): <= 420ms at p95 for 512-context requests.
2) Throughput/concurrency
   - Pilot target: sustain 120 qps with 8 concurrent connections (avg request size ~110 tokens).
3) Streaming behavior
   - Need sub-200ms first-byte for streaming starts, and steady per-token pacing for long streams (>1024 tokens).
4) Fallback policy
   - If GPU queue exceeds threshold, Redwood routing will fall back to quantized LLM variant; expected p95 latency increases noted in attachment.

Attachments: clarion_perf_map_v1.xlsx (pilot scenarios + load profiles), redwood_slo_proposal_v2.pdf (SLO buckets + suggested canary thresholds).

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- By Fri 06/22: Clarion to share representative request traces (anonymized) and success criteria confirmation.
- Week of 06/25: Redwood runs a targeted performance sweep against their traces in our Dedicated sandbox (dry-run).
- Week of 07/02: Joint pilot: 2-week pilot with telemetry access, build in canary gating.

Can you confirm the criteria above and whether procurement needs anything ahead of the pilot? If you prefer a short 20-minute follow-up to lock the data sample format, happy to set that up.

Thanks —
Rohan

rohan.mehta@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks Rohan — useful summary. A couple clarifications from our engineering and procurement sides: 

- On latency: our internal SLA to product is p95 <= 450ms for 95% of calls; the 420ms number looks good but we need Redwood to show a 450ms p95 at our representative load to accept.
- On throughput: 120 qps peak is aggressive during business hours; our current estimate is 80-100 qps for initial rollout. Can Redwood target a 100 qps steady-state and show headroom for bursts to 140 qps?
- Streaming first-byte: sub-200ms is critical for our UX.

Procurement note: before pilot we need a short note on data retention (logs + KV cache TTL) and whether any PII will be stored. I'll loop procurement explicitly.

Attached: sample_trace_anon.json (we'll send via your shared drive link).

Ayesha

- Latency: our Dedicated sandbox with mid-2027 kernels reliably hits p95 ~380ms for 512-context on A100-equivalent with batching disabled; with request batching typical p95 moves toward 410-430ms. We should propose demonstrating at both their stated steady-state (100 qps) and at a burst profile (140 qps).
- Throughput: propose we offer a pilot config that targets 100 qps sustained and validates burst to 140 qps (2-minute bursts). We must include KV cache hints and a recommended batching window; Tessa, can you prepare the pilot runbook snippet?
- Data retention: procurement wants data retention specifics. Lauren, can you share the short bullet list for retention + PII handling (KMS/HSM mention + cache TTL policy)?

I'll draft a concise reply to Clarion by EOD after we include Tessa and Lauren's inputs.

Hi all —

Thanks for the notes, Ayesha. Quick pilot runbook excerpt and commitments from Redwood (summary):

Pilot configuration (targeting Clarion requirements):
- Pilot duration: 2 weeks (14 calendar days)
- Topology: 3x GPU nodes (dedicated pool) configured with dynamic batching off for p95-sensitive flows, KV cache enabled with 6-hour TTL for warm prefixes.
- Targets we will measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-byte streaming latency, sustained qps (100) and burst qps (140 for 2-minute windows).
- Acceptance thresholds for go/no-go:
   * p95 single-turn latency at 100 qps: <= 450ms (must meet to be green)
   * streaming first-byte: <= 200ms at p95
   * sustained qps: 100 qps with <1% error rate

Data & compliance notes (short bullets for procurement):
- No PII persisted by default in model KV or logs; any customer-provided traces will be stored only for the pilot evaluation window (30 days) and then auto-deleted unless Clarion requests otherwise.
- All at-rest data encryption via KMS; access logs are viewable in Console and can be exported for audit.
- We can provide SOC2 artifacts as part of the procurement packet (we'll attach to HubSpot link).

Next steps (action items):
- Clarion: confirm you will upload anonymized traces to the shared drive link by EOD Fri 06/22.
- Redwood (Tessa): prepare pilot runbook snippet and a short checklist for the telemetry dashboard by Mon 06/25.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare cost estimate for the 2-week pilot (reserved nodes + telemetry access) and include optional extended retention add-on.

If that looks good we can reply to Clarion and propose a 20-min sync Mon 06/25 to confirm trace format.

Cheers —
Tessa Morgan
